evidence: Conditional scene selection from one saved CM1 equatorial ring, second lunar cycle. It is not a global optimum, regional weather forecast or climate-occurrence statistic.

earth-open.json.reading_rule: Cloud selection uses qc+qi >= 1e-5 kg/kg; tops are cell centres, not scale heights. Optical follow-up includes all five condensates. Clear-overhead selection is not zero optical depth. Native-water admission and finite-source optical transmission are separate checks.

rejected.reason: Coarse model water mask disagreed with native ground roughly 3152 m above the atlas water. Rejected as an offshore view; no separate perched lake was assumed.
Earth ray transmission was acceptable but vertical all-condensate optical depth was about 7.57: too overcast for the requested open cloud scene.
High cloud top alone was misleading; vertical all-condensate optical depth was about 19.96.

interpretation: Candidate screening uses qc+qi >= 1e-5 kg/kg for cloud presence and all five hydrometeors for vertical opacity. Tops are model cell-centre altitudes, not atmospheric scale heights.
The Earth mode covers 15 to 80 E; final native-water admission is limited to the available equatorial 0 to 180 E strip. Other regional study cases were reviewed but not globally resimulated.
The tighter twilight screen returned no candidates in this sample, not proof that such clouds cannot occur.
Cloud placement and texture outside the 2-D ring remain conditional; the optical scene assumes 100 km cross-ring extent.
